picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 4 Ohio State is looking for revenge against No. 5 Indiana after last year's Big Ten title game Getty Images The 100th all-time meeting between Ohio State and Indiana should be a good one. The fifth-ranked Hoosiers host the fourth-ranked Buckeys with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to Indianapolis. The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warmup for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. It managed just 94 rushing yards against Texas in Week 2. Kent State held the Buckeyes to 3.8 yards per carry. You get the idea. picks.headline: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History
picks.blurb: Rece Davis Reveals Ohio State-Indiana Pick for 'Biggest Game' in Bloomington History Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis picked Ohio State to win at Indiana on Saturday, siding with the Buckeyes in a top-five showdown that puts the Hoosiers’ 22-game winning streak on the line in Bloomington. On the College GameDay podcast, Davis joined fellow panelists Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel in taking No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) over No. 5 Indiana (6-0), though he expects a close finish. “I think a field goal at the end decides it one way or the other,” Davis said. Rece Davis explains his Ohio State pick Ohio State head coach Ryan Day takes the team out of the tunnel before the game against the Maryland Terrapins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. Davis called Saturday’s noon ET kickoff on Fox the “ biggest game in the history of Bloomington , Indiana, not played on a basketball court.” It’s a rematch of last December’s Big Ten championship game, which Indiana won 13-10 in Indianapolis on its way to the national title. His case against the Hoosiers rests on the streak itself. “When you have a winning streak as long as Indiana’s, longest in the country ... you start having these near misses,” Davis said. “Sooner or later, one gets you, and it can almost reset you a little bit.” Indiana held off Northwestern 29-23 in its Big Ten opener after starting running back Turbo Richard left with an injury, leaning on backup Lee Beebe Jr. for 203 rushing yards. Last Saturday in Lincoln, Indiana trailed Nebraska 17-6 in the fourth quarter before quarterback Josh Hoover hit receiver Nick Marsh for touchdowns of 75 and 44 yards, the second on fourth-and-1. Afterward, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said his players “ took a deep breath and relaxed and forgot all the garbage in the first half.” Can Ohio State protect Julian Sayin? Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin (10) throws during the college football game against the Maryland Terrapins | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Davis pointed to the Buckeyes’ offensive line as the deciding matchup. “Ohio State has allowed pressure on 27% of its dropbacks this season. That’s 14th in the Big Ten,” Davis said. “That’s not a great formula against Indiana. Indiana does an unbelievable job of getting pressure without blitzing.” Indiana leads the Big Ten with 20 sacks, while Ohio State has allowed 11, which ranks 14th in the conference . The Hoosiers also finished last December’s 13-10 win with five sacks and nine tackles for loss. Still, the Buckeyes have done damage when the pocket holds. Quarterback Julian Sayin, who holds No. 1 in our Big Ten quarterback rankings , has thrown for 1,772 yards and 17 touchdowns, and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdown catches. Ohio State’s offense also ranks second nationally in expected points added per pass, while Indiana’s defense ranks 76th in that measure. And the Buckeyes’ line landed on the Joe Moore Award midseason honor roll on Wednesday. Why Davis still backs Indiana’s offense Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover (10) passes against the Nebraska Cornhuskers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. Davis pushed back on the idea that Indiana’s attack has slipped, comparing Hoover to Fernando Mendoza, who quarterbacked the Hoosiers to last season’s title. “If Josh Hoover plays 16 games, as Fernando did last year, the numbers are going to be pretty much the same, almost the same,” Davis said. “He’s thrown 17 touchdown passes. I think Fernando finished with 41 last year. You double that to the end of the season, you’re at 34, and then you have the playoff.” Davis also noted that Indiana remains a run-first team. “Turbo Richard leads the conference in runs of 20 yards or longer,” he said. “They average over six yards a carry.” He placed the matchup in rare Big Ten company, too. “Only once have two teams played three consecutive seasons and been in the top five of the AP poll in all three meetings: Michigan and Ohio State in the middle of the legendary Ten-Year War between Bo Schembechler and Woody Hayes,” Davis said. ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took the opposite side this week, picking Indiana as the underdog to extend its streak to 23 games. picks.blurb: This week is another major test for the No. 4 Ohio State Buckeyes, who go on the road to face the No. 5 Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. During his weekly press conference on Monday, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti praised Ohio State’s talent and coaching staff. “We’re playing a great team this week at home in Ohio State. They’re a great football team with a lot of great players, and they’re extremely well coached. Ryan Day does a great job, and both coordinators and all the position coaches are really, really good,” said Cignetti . Cignetti, Day Trade Praise Ahead of Ohio State-Indiana Showdown Later in his press conference, Cignetti talked about facing an Ohio State program that’s used to winning championships. “Winning does a lot of good things, and I think that’s what’s happened. You’ve got an opponent coming in here that’s used to winning and winning championships, and there isn’t a stronger brand in America than Ohio State football,” Cignetti said . “It’s been that way for years and years. We’re a team that’s still developing, and I’m sure they’d say the same thing about their team. It ought to be a great environment.” During his press conference, Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day said this weekend’s game against Indiana will be a huge challenge. “It’s going to be a huge challenge. They do an excellent job up front on defense,” Day said. “Their defensive line is one of the biggest challenges we’ll have all season.” When asked about Indiana star wide receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, Day was very complimentary. “These guys in particular are very clean route runners,” Day said . “They’re really strong on contact, have really good body control, have run-after-the-catch ability. “Certainly, Becker has made some big-time plays in big-time moments, and Marsh is playing as good as anybody right now. This is a huge challenge for our secondary.” With both coaches bracing for a tight game, Mark Followill shared his pick with Ohio State Buckeyes on SI . Mark Followill Picks Ohio State in a Near Coin Flip In an exclusive interview, Mark Followill, the TV play-by-play voice of the Dallas Mavericks and a Big Ten Network broadcaster who called Ohio State’s win over Maryland last weekend, gave his prediction for Saturday’s top-five showdown and explained why he’s leaning toward the Buckeyes. “To me, this is a very even matchup. But when in doubt, because of what I’ve seen in person and what I saw of his performances in the lead-up to the game, I’m going to lean toward the team that’s got the best player on the field,” Followill said. “I don’t want to say he can win the game single-handedly, but if the game is in the balance, he’s more likely than anyone else to make a game-tipping play." He went on to say that he likes Indiana's team as well, but Ohio State's playmakers make it difficult to sway his opinion on where the result will go. “I like Indiana’s defense a lot. They can pressure the passer without having to sell out to do it. But Ohio State is showing me that, on top of having an explosive playmaker in Jeremiah Smith who can pop off a big play at any time, they can dominate the line of scrimmage and the run game even when their offensive line isn’t at full strength,” Followill said. “If you’ve got that, I’m going to roll with them.. "I think it’s going to be a fantastic freaking game. If you’re going to pin me down and force me to make a prediction, that’s the way I’m going to lean. I’ll give you 52-48.” The Buckeyes and Hoosiers kick off Saturday at 12 pm EDT at Memorial Stadium, with the game airing on FOX. away.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes
away.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. Doubtful: WR Brandon Inniss, RT Phillip Daniels, LB Christian Alliegro, DE Khary Wilder, RB Anthony Rogers The Block O captain for Ohio State, who has been quiet for the Buckeyes as they have opened Big Ten play, looks to not be available for this matchup where he could have been productive in what should be a big day for the Ohio State offense. Senior Phillip Daniels looks to be unavailable again, which should move Siereveld to that right tackle spot for another week and place Gabe VanSickle at guard for Ohio State. VanSickle fought some penalties problems last week at Iowa, and will be something to watch today. Riley Pettijohn and Tarvos Alford look to see more significant snaps today with Alliegro out today also. Khary Wilder has also been a name Ohio State fans have called out in wanting to see more snaps, but will not get that chance today. Manning's inconsistency has kept the Longhorns' offense largely out of rhythm this season, a critique he'll try to correct against the SEC's worst defense. After a loss to rival Oklahoma sent the Longhorns falling six spots in the AP Poll, Texas is hoping to use the tailspinning Gators as their punching bag to stay in the College Football Playoff picture. Florida has lost back-to-back SEC games in blowout fashion, tumbling out of the national rankings without a clear solution to stop the hemorrhaging. Sumrall said progress is sometimes "dysfunctional" and agreed with some of the booing he experienced on the sideline of last week's loss to South Carolina . The Gators struggled to block Gamecocks edge Dylan Stewart and now must endure the athleticism of Colin Simmons , who leads college football with 9.5 sacks. Simmons collected five sacks during a win at Tennessee last month and is the runaway favorite to win the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year honor. Texas vs. Florida: Need to know Turnovers and touchdowns: Manning's production against Power Four competition has been pedestrian -- four touchdown passes and four interceptions. Two came during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six that swung the game's momentum to the Sooners. Manning's been sacked 12 times through five games -- 10 coming against Ohio State , Tennessee and Oklahoma. If there's a get-right opportunity for Florida's defense, perhaps this is it. Frightening defensive numbers: Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense, explosive plays allowed, pass defense and 15th in scoring defense this season. Sumrall said this week he was taking a closer look at multiple areas of his team to try and fix what has nuked this 4-0 start for the Gators. It starts with getting stops on defense against the Longhorns. Longhorns' second 'revenge' game: A failure-to-show loss against the Gators in Gainesville ultimately kept Texas out of the CFP last year. Now, Sarkisian's squad has a chance to move to 2-0 this season in revenge opportunities after beating Ohio State in Week 2. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Texas starts a run of three straight home games, getting Ole Miss next and Mississippi State to follow. How is this only the sixth game between these two? Texas is 3-1-1, with the 7-7 tie coming in the first meeting in 1924. How To Watch Florida vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida Will Win The defense isn't getting fixed over the next few weeks, but that's part of what a rebuild is all about. The Gators win when the offense rocks, and the yards and points allowed are simply the cost of doing business. However, there's one key element to the Florida D that should show up huge. The pass rush is outstanding. The Gator defensive front averages close to three sacks and seven tackles for loss per game, and as good as Arch Manning is – seriously, he's really good, despite the popular opinions at the moment after the OU loss – he's still not amazing when he's getting rushed. The Texas offensive line has been better than last year for the ground game, but the pass protection has been a problem. Why Texas Will Win The Texas defense is going to stuff the Florida offense cold. Missouri and South Carolina never let Gator star Jadan Baugh and the running game breathe. The Gamecocks and Tigers combined for 18 tackles for loss against the Florida attack, and both allowed fewer than 400 yards of total offense. For all the problems in the meltdown against Oklahoma, the Texas defense was great. It allowed only 238 yards of Sooner offense, and for the fourth game in a row – including against Ohio State and Tennessee – the defense allowed fewer than 100 rushing yards. Florida vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines It turned out to be one of the most important games of the 2025 season. Florida finished the year 4-8, but one of those wins was a 29-21 thriller over Texas. The Longhorns lost on the road to both Ohio State and Georgia – no shame there against two teams that finished with 12 wins – but that loss to the Gators kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Yeah, Texas lost to Oklahoma, but weird things happen in the Red River Rivalry. Against Florida, the offense will keep it conservative, but Arch will connect on a few deep shots to push ahead. The defense will take care of the rest. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:36 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas looks to bounce back against Florida after a devastating loss to Oklahoma. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A reported crowd of approximately 10,000 fans filled Clark Field, the current location of the Caven Lacrosse and Sports Center across San Jacinto Boulevard from Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Central Texas connections: Senior TJ Shananan Jr. , a graduate of Westlake High School in Austin, has started all six games at right guard after spending two seasons at Texas A&M and one year at Penn State. Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs the ball during the Red River Rivalry game against Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When Texas has the ball This seems like a get-right game for Manning, who ranks seventh in the SEC with 224.4 yards a game on 63% passing with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) pulls off a broken facemark after an interception during the game against Texas State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Sep. 5, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Florida key matchup Texas center Connor Robertson vs. Florida noseguard Brendan Bett Brendan Bett, a 6-4, 320-pound transfer from Baylor, anchors the interior of the Gators' 3-4 front from his noseguard spot. He's been active with 15 total tackles and three tackles for a loss but doesn't play at the level of the linemen from Oklahoma, Ohio State or Tennessee. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. Texas vs Florida prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 34, Florida 16. Barring any more special teams disasters or unacceptable turnovers, the Longhorns should have too much firepower for a reeling Florida defense. Danny Davis: Texas. I doubt the offense will have solved all of its problems over the past week, and don't get me started on the special teams. But only minimal improvement from Arch's bunch will be necessary if the Longhorns continue to play well against the run and subdue Jadan Baugh. Cedric Golden: Texas 27, Florida 20. The Horns respond in favorable fashion but questions remain about this offense and its inability to run the ball. Michael Shapiro: Texas 35, Florida 20. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian will get his wish for a fast start with the Longhorns back at Royal-Memorial Stadium, where they enter Saturday eyeing their 24th victory in the last 25 home games. Kiffin called him "a huge part of our success there" this week. Now Mississippi State's head coach, he leads the Bulldogs into a top-25 showdown with LSU on Saturday. "I don't like playing against him because they go so fast," Kiffin said this week. LSU (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is reeling after an overtime loss at Kentucky last week, and finds itself in a familiar place under previous coaches: two losses at the midpoint of the season. It wasn't supposed to start this way for Kiffin, who took over a program with deep pockets and turned the roster over into one of the most talented in the country. A third conference loss in Kiffin's first season would leave almost no margin for November, with Alabama and Texas still coming to Baton Rouge. Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) has already won two SEC games, exceeding the one Lebby collected in his first two seasons combined. Alabama rode into Starkville and won 56-23 two weeks ago, and Kamario Taylor , the sophomore quarterback who spent September in the Heisman Trophy conversation, finished the day on the sideline with a boot on his right foot. Two weeks later, nobody outside the Bulldogs' building knows if he will play. Lebby said the SEC availability report would answer that question. LSU vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Kamario Taylor's right foot : Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards and an SEC-best 17 touchdowns with four interceptions. He's thrown three touchdowns in the last five games, the longest stretch since LSU's Jayden Daniels in 2023. He first hurt his foot in the win over Missouri , and it showed against the Tide. He was sacked five times and finished with minus-26 rushing yards before leaving the game. If he can't play, Lebby's options are redshirt freshman Parker Puckett and AJ Swann , who spent a season at LSU. Where is Mississippi State's ground game? Fluff Bothwell has 403 yards and three touchdowns on 74 carries, but he had only one carry against Alabama and spent most of the afternoon with a boot on his left foot. The Bulldogs were outrushed 179-18. Now they get a defense that ranked second nationally against the run through four weeks, allowing 47.5 yards per game. Kentucky found cracks last week. CJ Baxter broke a 77-yard run on the first snap and finished with 123 yards. The Wildcats ran for 155 yards. The Sam Leavitt Experience : LSU QB Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,496 yards and 10 touchdowns, but he has thrown an interception in every game this season, totaling eight through six games. No one in the FBS has thrown more interceptions. At Kentucky, he completed 25 of 34 passes for 275 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another in overtime, but he also threw a pick and lost a fumble on a sack in the fourth quarter. LSU's recent success : The Tigers have won the last three meetings against Mississippi State. The Bulldogs last won in Baton Rouge in 2020, when they pulled off a 44-34 upset in Mike Leach's first season. This is the first meeting since 2023. The teams used to play each other annually, but that ended when the SEC expanded to 16 teams in 2024. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. away.blurb: Taylor was listed on Mississippi State's initial SEC availability report Wednesday as questionable for Saturday's showdown against the 21st-ranked Tigers as he continues to deal with an undisclosed lower-leg injury. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. LSU. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . Whether the Bulldogs will have starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center remains uncertain. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. The Tigers have had some rough injury luck this season, but things have begun to slow down, mercifully. Here are the initial reports put out by the conference on Wednesday night: No major surprises for LSU on this update. Majorly, they've avoided any more long-term injuries since the flurry a couple of weeks ago (knock on wood). Ideally, that OUT list will begin to shrink over the next month. Singleton being questionable stings in terms of depth if he isn't able to go. Davhon Keys has been the starter, but Singleton is expected to play as well. He was only able to play three snaps last week. Ideally, he'll be able to bounce back in time for this one to help out the linebacker room. This was pretty much the expected outcome for Taylor, after reports started leaking out earlier in the week . He hasn't had a full practice since that game against the Tide on Oct. 3, dealing with a foot issue. More Videos The LSU Tigers are searching for a bounceback against the Mississippi State Bulldogs this weekend and are going to have their eyes peeled on the injury report. Everyone is awaiting the Friday status of Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor, who has been dealing with an injury suffered against the Alabama Crimson Tide. He has been one of the most electric quarterbacks in the entire country, and the Bulldogs don't have a great answer as a backup. If he doesn't go, it would likely be redshirt freshman walk-on Parker Puckett. No offense to Puckett, but Blake Baker's defense would be licking its chops after that news. The uncertainty around Taylor is likely a large reason why LSU is favored by over two touchdowns, rising since the lines opened as well. Bothwell also suffered an injury against Alabama, which was another big loss for their offense. He had three straight games with at least 100 yards and is picking up 5.4 yards per carry. The backups combined for 37 yards on 20 carries in last week's game. They will be watching his status closely as well.

picks.headline: Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) directs teammate running back Nick Peal (30) during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. picks.blurb: Auburn vs Georgia Prediction: Can the No. 1 Team Play Like It? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Auburn vs Georgia Prediction: Can the No. 1 Team Play Like It? Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:26 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There are rivalries, and there's the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry that started in 1892 – only Minnesota vs Wisconsin has gone on longer than Auburn vs Georgia. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. How To Watch Auburn vs Georgia Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Auburn Will Win The Auburn defense has been great. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. picks.blurb: Georgia Bulldogs vs. Auburn Tigers final score predictions: Can Alex Golesh get his first upset-rivalry win over the No. 1 team in the country? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton Auburn Tigers QB Byrum Brown Randy Sartin-Imagn Images David Leong-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 4:09 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs are in a terrific spot, but they'll face one of their biggest rivals, the Auburn Tigers. The Georgia Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn is a team that's trying to turn their program around. And, Alex Golesh is looking for that first unranked-upset win over a rival. Can he get it done on Saturday? A to Z Sports' experts picked the final scores for this game. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. Their win over Alabama is about as good as it gets for any team this season, other than maybe Texas beating Ohio State. But, they have to show they can be consistent. And, there are definitely still things to work on. As for Auburn, this offense has not been as fun to watch as we all maybe thought it would in the offseason. But Georgia has the mix of defense and offense that Auburn just simply won't be able to hang around with. Then again, this is a rivalry game, and we've seen some weird things happen in rivalry games this year alone. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games BULLDOGS-EXTRA Georgia football vs Auburn scouting report, bold predictions, injury updates Marc Weiszer Athens Banner-Herald Oct. 15, 2026, 4:02 a.m. ET At the end of a profanity-filled postgame speech leaked after Georgia’s football’ s win at Alabama Saturday night—audio that Kirby Smart said he preferred had not been put on social media—the Bulldogs coach mentioned building off of it. “This team, man, are you going to take this and grow from it?” Smart said. “The naysayers said they couldn’t go there and win and they ain’t played nobody.” Alabama certainly was a step up in competition, a team the Bulldogs traded haymakers with all night in a 20-17 victory. The challenge for Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC) this week is to turn the page from an opponent that now feels like a rivalry to many to one that has been one of the biggest and is its longest in Auburn . This is the 131 st meeting between the schools some 180 miles apart. Auburn (4-2, 1-2) will have a fourth different head coach on the sideline since Smart came aboard in Athens. Smart has gone up against Gus Malzahn, Bryan Harsin, Hugh Freeze and now will face Alex Golesh. The Tigers are ranked No. 33 on ESPN’s SP+, which puts it 11 th in the SEC and below an Oklahoma team that Georgia rolled past three weeks ago. The Tigers had an open date on their schedule last week, giving the players a break from the grind and coaches more of a chance to evaluate how to get better. “They're coming off an off week, and we're coming off a really tough physical game,” Smart said. “It will be really important that the mindset and the approach to the game is right because they want to make it physical the way they play.” Georgia vs. Auburn predictions Georgia is No. 1 ranked for the first time since September of 2024. It moved to that spot a day after top-ranked Texas was upset by unranked Oklahoma. Two other top 15 SEC teams also went down to unranked foes: No. 10 LSU to Kentucky and No. 15 Florida to South Carolina. Smart alluded to those results when talking about the challenge Auburn presents. “They have a lot of talent,” Smart said. “They've got good football players, and it's any given Saturday in this conference, as we see every week.” Auburn is missing perhaps its most valuable piece. Linebacker Xavier Atkins, a second-team All-American in 2025, won’t play. Golesh didn’t disclose why saying that would be kept “in-house,” and his status would be revisited next week. AuburnSports reported Atkins has had disciplinary issues centered on being late to or missing mandatory meetings and practice habits were also a factor. Georgia players have said putting the last game behind them is just part of what they do. “We try to focus on being consistent,” linebacker Justin Williams said. “You know you can’t be too high or too low. You have to be right in the middle.” Georgia vs. Auburn scouting report Why Georgia has an advantage: Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown ranks 14th in the SEC in passing efficiency and has as many interceptions as touchdowns with 7 each. "We've got the right plan in place to go attack them," he told reporters in Auburn. The Bulldogs defense limited Alabama to 346 total yards. Why Auburn has an advantage: The Tigers have been solid on the back end, ranking 30th in the nation in pass efficiency defense with 6 interceptions and just 4 touchdown passes against. UCLA transfer Andre Jordan has 2 interceptions. Linebacker Elijah Melendez (3 sacks) and Walter Mathis Jr. (2 sacks) from Savannah help apply the pressure. Georgia vs. Auburn injury updates Georgia: Wide receiver Isiah Canion (lower extremity, out), running back Chauncey Bowens (lower body, out), safety KJ Bolden (leg, questionable), wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (collarbone, out), defensive back Tyriq Green (leg, out), offensive lineman Marcus Harrison (undisclosed, probable), RB Dante Dowdell (multiple injuries including collarbone, lung and arm, out), outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee, out). Auburn: Offensive lineman Tai Buster (undisclosed, out), TE Hunter Herring (undisclosed out), LB Xavier Atkins (non-injury, out). Georgia 37, Auburn 10: Auburn last topped 13 points in a game at Georgia in 2009 when Chris Todd was the quarterback. This doesn't look like a Tigers offense that can change that. It has scored 21 and 14 points the last two games and ranks 13th in the SEC in scoring. Georgia vs. Auburn scouting report: What we're watching Georgia pass rush: Georgia rang up four sacks against Alabama, raising its season total to 17. That's just three shy of what the Bulldogs registered all of last season. Raylen Wilson leads the team with 3, Chris Cole has 2 1/2 and Gabe Harris contributes 2. Cole's 14 quarterback pressures leads the team. Auburn's pace: The Tigers are apt to snap the ball fast, something that Georgia cornerback Demello Jones noted this week. Auburn leads the nation in running a play every 21.5 seconds, the fastest in the nation. "It's something we've got to adjust to," Jones said. "Just us getting lined up on the defensive side, executing calls." Georgia RB Bo Walker: Georgia still is not at full strength in the backfield. Dwight Phillips carried the load at Alabama with 17 rushes for 120 yards but second-year running back Bo Walker had a career-high 10 carries for 69 yards. He showed good vision and big-play ability on a day where his longest run was 37 yards. "He brings a lot," Phillips said. "He's explosive as well." Homecoming game for Auburn tight end: Jake Johnson, in his fifth college season after playing for Texas A&M and North Carolina, returns home to face Georgia. Johnson is the son of former NFL coach Brad Johnson and is the nephew of former Georgia coach Mark Richt. The Oconee County High graduate has 7 catches for 43 yards this season. Bold predictions for Georgia football vs Auburn Georgia will continue ground game momentum: Georgia's offensive line limited Alabama to one sack last week and paved the way for 206 rushing yards. Auburn is 81st against the run nationally at 149 yards per game and gave up touchdown runs of 25 and 44 in its last game at Tennessee. Byrum Brown will make plays with his feet: The South Florida transfer has more rushing yards per game than any quarterback in the SEC with 68.8 per game and has 4 rushing touchdowns. Byrum is a load to bring down at 6-foot-3 and 235 pounds. He rushed for 107 yards at Tennessee on 19 carries. London Humphreys will continue to be key target: After having just four catches in the first four games, the Vanderbilt transfer has 6 catches for 62 yards the last two weeks including a 20-yard touchdown catch at Alabama from Gunner Stockton. Auburn's offensive line will be rattled on the road: In Auburn's only road game this season, the Tigers had a bevy of pre-snap penalties involving four different offensive lineman. Georgia's crowd should be able to cause false starts for the Tigers once again for an offensive line filled with transfers.

away.blurb: The remaining SEC teams in the AP Poll are Ole Miss (No. 9), Missouri (No. 13), Tennessee (No. 14), and Mississippi State (No. 16). The Florida Gators are out of the polls after losing to South Carolina last Saturday, 38-19. In the latest AP Top 25 , Georgia jumped to the top spot after defeating No. 6 Alabama 20-17. The former No. 1 team, Texas, was defeated by unranked Oklahoma 27-24 on Saturday and dropped six spots to No. 7. The last time Auburn played the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 was in 2023, when it lost to the Georgia Bulldogs 27-20 in Hugh Freeze's first year as head coach. The last time the Tigers defeated the top-ranked team was in 2017, beating Alabama 26-14. Two weeks before that game, Auburn defeated Georgia, 40-17, when the Bulldogs were ranked No. 1. The AP Poll saw some movement outside of Texas dropping six spots. The LSU Tigers fell the farthest, dropping from No. 10 to No. 22 after their 35-34 overtime loss to unranked Kentucky. However, that win by the Wildcats put them in the rankings at No. 15. Despite losing to Georgia, Alabama stayed at No. 6. home.headline: Kirby Smart says Georgia is 'beat up.' Here's the latest on injuries
home.blurb: “We're a beat up football team right now, guys,” coach Kirby Smart said after the 20-17 win over Alabama. “We've got guys out left and right.” Canion was listed as questionable last week on the SEC Availability Report before being downgraded Friday to out. Blackshear is out with a broken collarbone, according to ABC on Saturday night’s broadcast. The average return to play for contact sports for a broken collarbone is 8 to 12 weeks, according to an Instagram post by Dr. Mike Galbraith, a Texas-based sports medicine physician. Freshman Craig Dandridge played a season-high 55 snaps with Blackshear and Canion out. "We had to go all week kind of not knowing on Isiah," Smart said Monday. "How does it affect you? You talk to Mike (Bobo), you talk to the offensive staff, it's frustrating because you don't really know who's in and who's out. You're trying to make decisions. We thought Nate was going to be able to play. That was a surprise to us. Isiah, we knew it would be close, maybe or maybe not. It just makes it hard because you can't get enough reps for guys." The No. 1 Bulldogs are dealing with several notable injuries heading into a week seven game Saturday at home against Auburn. Georgia played its third straight game without Isiah Canion, the transfer wide receiver from Georgia Tech who Smart said Monday is dealing with "a lower extremity injury." The Bulldogs were also without wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, who was injured in the win over Vanderbilt on Oct. 3. Phillips rushed for a career-high 120 yards on 17 carries against Alabama with Frazier and Chauncey Bowens sidelined. Bowens leads the team in rushing touchdowns. He sustained an undisclosed injury against Vanderbilt. Frazier missed the Oklahoma game after being injured at Arkansas and returned to get two second-half carries against Vanderbilt. He was not listed on the availability report all last week, but warmed up and did not play Saturday. ABC’s Holly Rowe said he made a quick cutting move and needed attention from the training staff. Phillips was asked Monday if he had an idea that Frazier wouldn’t be able to go or was surprised. “That’s probably a Kirby Smart question,” he said with a smile.

The challenge for Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC) this week is to turn the page from an opponent that now feels like a rivalry to many to one that has been one of the biggest and is its longest in Auburn . This is the 131 st meeting between the schools some 180 miles apart. Auburn (4-2, 1-2) will have a fourth different head coach on the sideline since Smart came aboard in Athens. Smart has gone up against Gus Malzahn, Bryan Harsin, Hugh Freeze and now will face Alex Golesh. Two other top 15 SEC teams also went down to unranked foes: No. 10 LSU to Kentucky and No. 15 Florida to South Carolina. home.blurb: Jorden Edmonds, DB — Game-time decision Josh Ford, TE — Game-time decision Isiah Canion, WR — Questionable Ford is expected to be available to face Georgia, ESPN's Pete Thamel shared on College GameDay from Coleman Coliseum. Ford was reportedly doing pushups at practice on Tuesday despite the Sunday arm surgery. Alabama right tackle Jayvin James is not featured on the availability report. James left the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early with a lower extremity injury, and it forced him to sit out of the Mississippi State victory. Nevertheless, DeBoer said during Monday's press conference that he's "optimistic that [James] can return this week." He's good to go and is listed as the starting right tackle on the depth chart. It was reported a couple of weeks before the season that 5-star freshman cornerback Jorden Edmonds would miss some time due to a lower body injury. DeBoer said on Monday that "there’s a chance he can come back here, even in the regular season." That said, he was listed as questionable on the initial availability report. Edge rushers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu have missed the Crimson Tide's past two games and they'll be out once again. Hill has a lower-extremity injury and Umeozulu has turf toe. Hill and Umeozulu are the second and third Wolf linebackers on Alabama's depth chart. DeBoer shared the latest on these two as well, stating that Umeozulu will take "probably a couple more weeks," and Hill will "be back this season, but more than likely not this week." LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Alabama looks to recover from its first loss of the season on Saturday at No. 14 Tennessee Getty Images A pair of historic rivals with playoff aspirations are squaring off in a top-15 SEC showdown on Saturday, as No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for the Third Saturday in October. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory.
