picks.blurb: Alabama @ Tennessee Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Alabama @ Tennessee Preview And Prediction Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre (12) hands the ball to Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop (18) during a college football game between Tennessee and Auburn at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Oct. 3, 2026. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for a massive SEC rivalry showdown. Can Keelon Russell bounce back and keep the Tide's playoff hopes alive? One of college football's greatest rivalries returns Saturday afternoon as No. 6 Alabama (5-1) travels to Knoxville to face No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) in the Third Saturday in October showdown. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, and both programs have plenty to prove. Alabama is coming off a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia, while Tennessee narrowly escaped Arkansas with a 24-17 victory. The Crimson Tide defeated Tennessee 37-20 last season, but the Volunteers have won the last two meetings in Knoxville. With both teams fighting for College Football Playoff positioning, Saturday's matchup could have enormous consequences. Alabama: Can Keelon Russell Bounce Back? Alabama's offense has been one of the nation's most explosive units, averaging 44.2 points per game. Quarterback Keelon Russell has thrown for 1,599 yards, 12 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while adding 225 rushing yards and four scores. However, Georgia exposed some weaknesses in the sophomore quarterback's game. Russell completed just 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and one touchdown against the Bulldogs, struggling to consistently move the football against an elite defense. Saturday presents another difficult challenge. Tennessee is allowing just 15.5 points per game and has surrendered only three passing touchdowns through six games. Making matters worse, Alabama is expected to be without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who has recorded 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. That means Lotzeir Brooks, who has 389 receiving yards, and Rico Scott will need to step up. The Crimson Tide must also establish their rushing attack to prevent Tennessee from putting all its attention on Russell. Tennessee: The Volunteers Have a MAJOR Problem Tennessee has managed to win five of its first six games, but Josh Heupel's offense has serious questions at quarterback. Freshman Faizon Brandon has battled a shoulder injury, forcing George MacIntyre into his first career start against Arkansas. MacIntyre completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. And against Alabama's talented secondary, those mistakes could prove extremely costly. The Volunteers rank just 110th nationally in passing offense, averaging 186.5 yards per game. However, Tennessee has been outstanding on the ground. Running back DeSean Bishop has rushed for 678 yards and eight touchdowns, helping Tennessee average 228.3 rushing yards per game. Bishop will be the biggest threat to Alabama's defense, especially considering Georgia rushed for more than 200 yards against the Crimson Tide last weekend. Wide receiver Mike Matthews, who leads Tennessee with 396 receiving yards, could also create problems if Alabama becomes too focused on stopping the run. How Each Team Wins For Alabama, the formula starts with forcing Tennessee to throw the football. If the Crimson Tide can contain Bishop and put the Volunteers into third-and-long situations, their defense should have opportunities to create turnovers. Offensively, Russell must protect the football, utilize his mobility, and attack Tennessee's secondary without forcing unnecessary throws. For Tennessee, everything revolves around establishing the rushing attack and controlling possession. The Volunteers must also generate consistent pressure on Russell and prevent Alabama from creating explosive plays downfield. A loud Neyland Stadium crowd could make things difficult for Alabama, particularly if Tennessee establishes an early lead. I expect a physical, defensive battle between two SEC rivals. Tennessee's rushing attack will create problems early, but I don't trust the Volunteers' quarterback situation against Alabama's defense. Whether it's Brandon or MacIntyre under center, Tennessee simply hasn't demonstrated enough consistency throwing the football. Russell should respond with a much cleaner performance after struggling against Georgia, although I don't expect Alabama's offense to put up its usual explosive numbers. The Crimson Tide will establish a narrow lead before halftime and gradually take control in the second half. I expect Alabama's defense to force multiple turnovers, while Russell makes enough plays to secure a comfortable road victory. Final Score: No. 6 Alabama 24, No. 14 Tennessee 13 Alabama gets back on track, improves to 6-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Tennessee's quarterback struggles ultimately prove too much to overcome. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide

home.headline: Alabama dealt unfortunate injury news ahead of Tennessee clash
home.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide will look to bounce back after a razor close loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in Week 6 when they face off against the Tennessee Volunteers. But unfortunately, they will not be at full strength offensively in Saturday’s game. Junior wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been one of the more reliable and effective wide receivers in all of college football this season for the Crimson Tide. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. During their Week 6 loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams was forced to exit the game after both seemingly re-aggravating a knee injury in the game and suffering a concussion, which was what ultimately cut his game in Week 6 short. More news : Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor Vows to ‘Ruin’ LSU’s Night Leading up to the team’s Week 7 game, there was not much optimism that Coleman-Williams was going to be able to suit up for the game. And that reality was confirmed on Wednesday when Alabama released their weekly injury report, along with a report on the matter from Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. More news : UCLA HC Bob Chesney Drops Powerful Quote After Bruins’ Hot Start Considering Coleman-Williams leads the team in every major statistical category, including receptions (tied with Lotzeir Brooks), receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns, his absence on Saturday will almost certainly be missed. Add in the fact that the Tennessee Volunteers allow just 161.3 passing yards per game to opposing teams, the second-lowest passing yards allowed to opponents in the SEC, and it could very well be a tough day for Alabama star quarterback Keelon Russell. Tennessee football coach Josh Heupel revealed that the decision about the Vols' starting quarterback for Arkansas was made at the beginning of the week, but they're going to "play it by ear" going forward. Sophomore George MacIntyre got his first career start and led the No. 14 Vols to a 24-17 win over Arkansas on Oct. 10 in their first SEC road game. MacIntyre finished the Auburn game on Oct. 3 after freshman Faizon Brandon was benched during the second quarter. Brandon is dealing with a right shoulder injury, which he suffered during the 20-17 loss to Texas on Sept. 26. "Just with what he was dealing with, (Brandon) really didn't rep during the course of the week," Heupel said after the Arlansas win. I know most of you guys are tired of me saying that, but that's the truth of it. And we'll keep growing and going." Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. away.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers’ biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they’re already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. away.headline: Injury update: Will Mario Craver play today for Texas A&M against Missouri?
away.blurb: Texas A&M star receiver Mario Craver has been listed as questionable all week against the Missouri Tigers, as he continues to recover from some bangs and bruises he has sustained throughout the season thus far. With the release of this morning's SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report , that status appears to remain for Craver with kickoff now under an hour and a half away. Craver is listed as a game-time decision for the Aggies in this report, meaning that fans will be sweating his status heading right up into the game. Craver's skill set makes him one of the toughest matchups for A&M's opponents on the entire team, so having him ready and available for the Aggies is key in this matchup. There are some positive signs for Craver going into this game, though: he was spotted heading out to warm up against the Tigers, potentially signaling that he will be ready to go. Warmups are warmups, but if he was trending towards not playing, this would not be happening. This is a similar pattern, though, to what we saw against Arkansas last week. Craver was listed as questionable throughout the week and called a game time decision against the Hogs, but he eventually was ready to go and saw a good number of snaps in the first half. He didn't play much of the later part of the game, as it looked like he had tweaked something in the touches he did get. Maybe that was out of a sense of safety, though, as the Aggies had the game well in hand by halftime, and were much more committed to the run than they were the pass against the Hogs. He eventually left the game with an apparent injury , though he did return later on in the contest. There was a similar story the following week against LSU, however: he was targeted a lot earlier on in the game, but eventually had to leave with some sort of injury before returning. Especially with Terry Bussey out, though, Craver's availability is paramount. There was a good showing from TK Norman last week, who looks ready to step into an increased role, but there's a big difference between Arkansas at home and Missouri on the road. Those numbers don't fully illustrate his importance to quarterback Marcel Reed and an Aggies passing attack that's struggled to find consistency. And with Texas A&M desperately needing another SEC victory, the timing couldn't be worse. Craver's availability has been a concern for two consecutive weeks. His most productive performance came against Kentucky on September 19, when he caught 11 passes for 119 yards. That game demonstrated how heavily the Aggies can lean on Craver when their passing offense gets rolling. During the 2025 season, Craver established himself as one of Texas A&M's top receiving threats, catching 59 passes for 917 yards and four touchdowns. That kind of production is exactly what Reed could use against a Missouri team coming off an impressive 45-17 victory over Florida. The uncertainty surrounding Craver is particularly troubling because Texas A&M has already lost Terry Bussey for the remainder of the season. Bussey suffered a serious lower-body injury against Kentucky, leaving the Aggies without one of their most versatile offensive playmakers. Losing Craver, even temporarily, would further challenge an offense that has struggled to develop a reliable passing rhythm against SEC competition. Reed enters Saturday with six touchdown passes and four interceptions this season, illustrating the uneven performances that have contributed to Texas A&M's 3-2 start. Head coach Mike Elko's Aggies enter the Missouri matchup at 1-2 in conference play after losses to Kentucky and LSU. Last week's convincing victory over Arkansas offered some encouragement, particularly with Texas A&M's renewed commitment to establishing the running game. home.headline: Ex-Rebels lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss
home.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren’t made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it’s worth noting that Simmons’ Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. “I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder,” tailback Jamal Roberts said. “We definitely can let them guys handle that.” No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. “The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is,” Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. “There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides.” “We talk about the joy of the journey,” Drinkwitz said. “That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don’t think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that.” Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers’ biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they’re already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou’s top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. “He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape,” Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. “They’re a total team,” Drinkwitz said. “We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game.” In Mizzou’s most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications, though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. The Seminoles cannot win this game if quarterback Darian Mensah is given a clean pock

away.headline: What Initial Injury Report Reveals About No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Status Against Seminoles
away.blurb: Players ruled out aren’t a surprise: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-body; Out for Season), running back CharMar ‘Marty’ Brown (Left knee; Out for Season), tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season), cornerback Ja’Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left knee), and cornerback Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (Left shoulder). Redshirt junior cornerback Damari Brown is another big piece returning. He logged just six snaps against Clemson; limited with an undisclosed injury. The Hurricanes’ secondary has faced the most adversity to start the season, but sophomore Bryce Fitzgerald moving from safety to cornerback and others stepping up, most notably freshman safety/nickelback JJ Dunnigan, have kept them above water. Meanwhile, the Seminoles have ruled out the following: running back Samuel Singleton Jr., 2ide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, linebacker Izayia Williams, and linebacker Daylen Green. Linebacker Noah LaVallee is listed as questionable. The freshman has only appeared in one game this season – against Central Arkansas. The former three-star recruit logged three total tackles, two solos and an assist, a tackle for loss, and two quarterback hits. Defensive tackle Darryll Desir, cornerback Zae Thomas, and left guard/center Paul Bowling are listed as probable. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead WNBA All-Defensive first team Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Caleb's return won't solve it all Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 16, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. picks.headline: How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas). picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Kentucky Wildcats final score predictions: Can the Sooners get back in the CFP discussion with a win? The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off of a huge win over the Texas Longhorns at the Cotton Bowl in the Red River Rivalry. The Kentucky Wildcats are coming off a huge overtime win over LSU. Both teams are on a high but are looking to improve their records on Saturday night. So, does the team in Kentucky that's maybe at its best as a program get the win? Or does Oklahoma get another ranked win and get back into the College Football Playoff conversation? Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 This feels almost like the clock striking midnight for Kentucky here, as much as it does for me, who's lived the last two weeks dangerously. Both teams are coming in off super highs from last week. Oklahoma clipped Texas 27-24 on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky walked off LSU 35-34 in overtime, their second straight walk-off overtime win, going for two and getting it on the final play. Honestly, in a vacuum, I trust Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey more than I trust OU's John Mateer. But Minchey is going up against a very good Oklahoma defense, while Mateer has a more navigable task when he has the ball. I still don't see points a plenty here, but Oklahoma forces a key turnover late, and that's enough with the home crowd in Norman to get a close and resume-boosting win at the season's midpoint. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 20 This could be one of the ugliest games on the schedule, with both teams struggling to find much offensive consistency. Oklahoma will have chances to pull away, but John Mateer’s chaotic style makes it hard to trust the Sooners to put together four clean quarters. Mateer can make spectacular plays, but mistakes and questionable decisions could give Kentucky the extra possessions it needs to hang around. Don't expect a shootout here. This game could come down to which team makes fewer costly mistakes in the fourth quarter. I'm buying a little bit of Kentucky magic in this one. Kenny Minchey comes through with a couple of clutch plays at the biggest moments, giving the Wildcats just enough offense to pull off a road upset. Kentucky might not look dominant, and it certainly won't be pretty, but this team finds a way to make things interesting when the game is on the line. Oklahoma has a chance to put the Wildcats away but can't quite finish the job, opening the door for Kentucky to steal a win in a close, low-scoring battle. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 16 Will Stein has the Wildcats on a heater right now, and he's doing it with the two things you want in Kentucky's place: confidence and guts. He's won two games this season because the Wildcats went for two at the end, and that kind of belief in your team will go a long way in establishing a foundation for your program. Things are different for the Sooners, who are coming off of a fantastic win in Red River. Even so, John Mateer can't do much other than throw shock, and he did that brilliantly on the final drive against Texas. I don't think Mateer will change overnight, and the Wildcats will take advantage of him enough to win. Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 14 This game suddenly looks much better than it did a week ago after both Kentucky and Oklahoma pulled off massive upsets last weekend. Red River can always get wonky, but few expected OU to beat the number one team in the nation given how the offense has played. Will Stein's Wildcats have gone from quietly looking like a good football team to potentially being one of the conference's better teams after just one loss to Alabama and a last-minute OT win over LSU. The truth, however, is that OU may have found something more than just some Red River magic. This will be arguably the hardest test of the year for Kenny Minchey, and the battle of the brains between Brent Venables and Will Stein will be notable, but I think Oklahoma will get the job done. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 17 The Oklahoma Sooners are almost ready to kick off their first SEC night game (excluding CFP games) since 2024. And this one should be big, with both teams riding an insane high after huge wins. The Kentucky Wildcats will give OU's defense fits. It will happen, and I know my score prediction probably doesn't show that, but I have OU getting a few takeaways in this one. Kentucky is going to do a bunch of pre-snap stuff that's going to confuse you. They are very good at that, but Brent Venables has his unit locked in right now. OU will win this game once again through the defense and special teams, with some little moments here and there from the offense. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! After the 17-15 loss to the now No. 12 UCLA Bruins (5-0, 3-0 Big Ten) inside Autzen Stadium and Moore looking to move off of concussion protocol, no more mistakes can be made if a third straight College Football Playoff appearance is to be made. The over/under is set at 52.5. The last time these two opponents met was in the 2017 campaign, resulting in a 42-35 victory for the Ducks in Eugene, Oregon. That's as long as Moore is fully cleared to suit back up after suffering a concussion in the 41-27 victory at the USC Trojans back on Sept. 26. If Moore doesn't, will Sheldon product Thomas receive his first career start with Oregon? Will an offensive play-caller change be made after first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer conjured up only 272 total yards from the press box? Under Mehringer, the Ducks committed a total of seven turnovers to the Bruins, tied for the most since their 30-24 loss to Indiana in the Pacific Northwest back on Sept. 11, 2004. Raiola struggled to take care of the ball against coach Bob Chesney's defense, completing only 6-of-19 passes for 43 passing yards, zero touchdowns, and two interceptions. Not to mention his one lost fumble. Oregon as a whole only went 1-for-12 on third downs and 0-for-2 on fourth downs. The turnovers on downs gave up two more too many opportunities for UCLA's three-headed monster in the backfield, fifth-year Wayne Knight, fifth-year Anthony Woods, and senior Jaivian Thomas, to extend drives and let the clock dwindle away. That running back trio combined for 150 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown on 35 carries. picks.headline: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. To prepare for that, NU is pushing its practices back a two hours and asking players to adjust their sleep schedules. “I had read some of the things that P.J. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. Colandrea, who carried the ball 17 times for 47 yards and a touchdown Saturday, is one player Rhule probably won't have to worry about getting ready to play. Despite Colandrea's heavy workload in Week 6, Rhule maintained his stance on trusting the quarterback to remain productive while making smart decisions to protect his health. "I want him to play," said Rhule. "Dante (Moore, Oregon's quarterback) got hurt sliding, you know? Other guys are getting hurt sliding as well. Would I like Anthony to run the ball out of bounds? Certainly, but he's also cutting back on the zone read and making that game 17-6." "If you have a Porsche, you better let it drive 180," he continued. "I know everything I say gets blown into a little tidbit; I'm not saying he's a Porsche; I'm just saying I think it would be unwise to have a player like Anthony and not let him play to his full ability." picks.headline: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska had Indiana bottled up until they didn't. College football games last 60 minutes for a reason, and the Cornhuskers ultimately couldn't hold on to a two-possession lead in the fourth quarter. As Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich prepares his unit for a road matchup against a capable Oregon offense Saturday night, he met with the media Tuesday to recap the Blackshirts' performance against the Hoosiers and preview the challenge ahead against the nation's 25th-ranked offense. Aurich knows his defense played well for much of Saturday's game. Even so, he sees an opportunity for the Blackshirts to learn from what went wrong. “An opportunity missed,” he said. “Haunting a little bit, but don’t let the game beat you twice. You take what you can; you learn from it. First year with these guys. I think it’s an excellent opportunity for us to understand what winning time is and how we perform in those moments.” As the Huskers prepare for Oregon, they'll need to make plays in critical moments to have a chance to pull off the upset. Indiana running back Lee Beebe Jr. is tackled by Nebraska defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. “I think we’ve taken steps,” he said. “Fundamentally, you’re seeing us play different coverages at a higher level and have a bunch of answers for some teams with a pretty hefty run game.” “Gonna be another great test this week,” he continued. “I think Oregon has a lot of great tools in the run game that we’re going to have to match up with well. I’m pleased where we are, but I don’t think we’re anywhere near where I think we can be still.” Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola carries the ball against UCLA. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Still, Aurich knows Oregon will maintain its offensive identity regardless of which quarterback earns the start. “At the core of who they are, they’re going to be who they are,” said Aurich. “They’re going to be 11 and 12 (personnel); they’re going to have play actions off of that. They’re going to have a little bit of RPO free access. They want to get their playmakers involved.” “As we navigate each quarterback, I don’t know if it’s necessarily adding this plan to here, but we pull the best matchups from what we plan against all their core stuff,” he continued. “It’s much more of a where on the call sheet are we pulling from rather than a separate plan (for each quarterback).” Ohio wide receiver Eian Pugh is tackled by Nebraska's Jamir Conn. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Most notably, starting safety Jamir Conn's availability remains a question. On Monday, head coach Matt Rhule called Conn the "lifeblood" of Nebraska's defense . If Conn can't play, Aurich said the solution won't necessarily be as simple as plugging in his backup. In fact, the Big Red may even dabble in different defensive packages. “As we kind of iron out what Jamir’s availability is going to be, if he’s not available, it’s going to be a great test for everybody else in that room,” said Aurich. “Who steps up and how we find the best combination of the best 11 players on the field.” “Let’s say, for whatever reason, someone wasn’t available; it’s not always that we have to replace them with a safety or a corner,” he continued. “What’s the best 11?” Defensive lineman Owen Stoudmire | Nebraska Athletics Given how well Nebraska's defensive line played against Indiana, the Huskers could look to add another player at the line of scrimmage Saturday night. Aurich didn't say that directly, but he praised several defensive linemen for their performances. Given how well Nebraska's defensive line played against Indiana, the Huskers could look to add another player at the line of scrimmage Saturday night. Aurich didn't say that directly, but he praised several defensive linemen for their performances. “He’s the man,” Aurich said of Boston College transfer Owen Stoudmire. “He’s like a centering force of that defensive line. There are a lot of personalities on the defensive line, in a great way, but Owen is just steady, man. He’s steady and doesn’t get moved.” Aurich also praised freshman defensive tackle Dylan Berymon for making an impact in a high-stakes game. “I’m jacked up that he came and impacted us, not in garbage time, in a Big Ten game,” he said. “Really, really pleased with him. I think you’re going to see his role continue to expand.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Whether Nebraska opts for a different defensive scheme or adjusts its personnel in the secondary, the Huskers will face one of the nation's most explosive offenses this week. Oregon fell 17-15 to the Bruins at home Saturday. Nebraska lost 20-17 to visiting Indiana as the Hoosiers rallied in the fourth quarter. Here's an early look at the Cornhuskers. Senior Anthony Colandrea has been the starter since transferring from UNLV in the offseason, taking over the position previously held by Oregon backup Dylan Raiola. The 6-foot, 200-pound dual-threat veteran has 37 career starts and was the 2025 Mountain West Conference offensive player of the year. He also spent two seasons at Virginia and was an honorable mention freshman All-American in 2023 at Virginia. In six games this season, Colandrea has completed 119 of 186 passes for 1,405 yards, 13 touchdowns and three interceptions. He's also second on the team in rushing with 296 yards and three scores on 55 carries. Last week against Indiana he was 25-of-43 passing for 264 yards and an interception and rushed 17 times for 47 yards with a 39-yard TD run. Other Nebraska offensive standouts The Cornhuskers' run game is averaging 213.8 and 2.6 TDs per game, and their 39.5 carries per game and 16 rushing touchdowns are second-most in the Big Ten. Freshman Jamal Rule leads the team with 386 yards and five scores in five games. Senior Mekhi Nelson also has 284 yards and four TDs on 60 carries, and nine catches for 148 yards and a TD. Junior Kwazi Gilmer, a transfer from UCLA, is Nebraska's leading receiver with 32 catches for 418 yards and six touchdowns. Junior Jacory Barney Jr. has 27 catches for 341 yards and two touchdowns. He has nine grabs for 108 yards against Indiana last Saturday. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning runs off at halftime as the Oregon Ducks host the UCLA Bruins on Oct. 10, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Defensive standouts for Nebraska Nebraska is allowing 15.2 points per game and 277.2 yards, including just 94.7 on the ground. The Cornhuskers held Indiana to 328 yards, with just 65 of those yards coming on the ground on 22 attempts. The Hoosiers entered the game ranked ninth nationally averaging 252.6 yards per game. Senior linebacker Owen Chambliss, a transfer from San Diego State, is the leading tackler with 31 in five games. Safeties Jamir Conn and Donovan Jones have two sacks each. Conn also has a team-high 5.0 tackles for loss, and Jones has 4.5 tackles for loss, three pass breakups and one interception. Linebacker Vincent Shavers Jr. also has two sacks. The last time the Ducks and Cornhuskers met These two teams haven't met since Willie Taggert was the Oregon coach and Justin Herbert the starting quarterback. The result on Sept. 9, 2017 was a 42-35 Ducks victory at Autzen Stadium. Oregon jumped out to a 28-point lead in the first half and then survived a scoreless second half to get its first win against Nebraska since 1953, ending a streak of five-straight losses. Herbert threw for 365 yards and three touchdowns, Royce Freeman rushed for 153 yards and two touchdowns and the defense had four interceptions.
